issues.title: q18 clustered agg bundle: batched run-interval registration + template state init
issues.hypothesis: After E0045 the q18 HAVING subquery (60M rows, ~29K chunks, 15M runs) spends ~69ms CPU (summed over threads) in RegisterRunInterval (radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp:813). It takes a global mutex and does a std::map insert per chunk, which is ~2.4us per chunk, so most of it is lock contention across 8 threads. It also spends 62-72ms in RowOperations::InitializeStates (row_aggregate.cpp:8), one indirect call per state for 15M states. E0046 (template-copy init alone) measured q18 ~-2%, inside the 5% noise. Batching the interval registration (one lock per 64 chunks) removes most of the contention. Combined with template init, that should take ~100ms CPU (~12ms wall of ~178ms) off q18, enough to clear noise.
issues.plan: 1) radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp: give RadixHTLocalSinkState a small pending-interval buffer (vector<pair<uint64_t,uint64_t>>, cap 64). In SinkClustered (:934), instead of calling RegisterRunInterval per chunk, first check the local buffer for overlap with the new interval, then append it. When the buffer is full, and always in Combine/before finalize (wherever lstate.intervals and the run stores are handed to gstate), flush: take run_intervals_lock once, check and insert every pending interval (same lower_bound/prev logic), and set run_intervals_overlap on any conflict. Keep the exact open-interval endpoints: do NOT merge (a,b),(b,c) into (a,c), because another thread's interval starting at boundary key b would look like a false overlap. Required correctness check: overlap is now detected up to 64 chunks late, after those runs were already streamed. Confirm that the overlap path (run_intervals_overlap -> MergeRunStores ~:989 / run source :1554) already routes streamed run stores through the normal combine when overlap is set. Today an overlap found by RegisterRunInterval already happens after earlier intervals were streamed, so this should hold; if it does not, add the fallback. Every flush must finish before any finalize reads run_intervals_overlap. 2) Re-apply the E0046 template-copy init in row_aggregate.cpp RowOperations::InitializeStates: for layouts where no aggregate has a destructor, and init does not depend on the address, initialize one template state block once (cache it on the layout or the HT), then memcpy it to each row's aggregate offset. Keep the per-aggregate path otherwise. 3) Tests: the clustered-agg tests, plus a test where two threads' chunks overlap late (e.g. a union of two sorted ranges), checked against SET disabled clustered path / a shuffled copy. A/B q18 with .timer (sum of 8 subqueries).
issues.expected_gain: q18 -4..-7% (~-0.5% geomean). Other GROUP BYs with many groups get a small gain from template init.
issues.generality: Any GROUP BY over input clustered on the first key (sorted/insert-ordered FK columns), and any hash aggregate creating many groups with destructor-free states (SUM/COUNT/MIN/MAX on numerics). Possible slowdown: input that overlaps late now streams up to 64 more chunks before it falls back.
issues.risk: Medium-low. The delayed overlap detection must be covered by the existing fallback, and the template memcpy must skip aggregates whose init is not a plain constant fill.
